newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker as market awaits Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker as market awaits Greenspan.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Monday, taking much of their direction from U.S. treasuries, as concern about Tuesday's public testimony by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan kept activity muted.

"There was some selling during the day but I don't think there's been very heavy volume," said Dawn Desjardins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada. "People are waiting until tomorrow when we're going to get that Humphrey-Hawkins testimony."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$118.66 to yield 6.566 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.54 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from two basis points at Friday's close.
"People are waiting for Humphrey-Hawkins and it's kind of a boring day," said one bond trader with a Canadian bank. "It's very low volume," the trader said.

The head of the U.S. Federal Reserve will begin his two-day, semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins economic report before Congress on Tuesday. Greenspan is expected to say that inflation may be down but not out and the central bank must remain wary of inflation pressures, traders said.
Aside from Greenspan's testimony, the Canadian bond market is looking ahead to a new 30-year Government of Canada bond supply.
The Bank of Canada on Wednesday will auction C$1.3 billion of 8.0 percent bonds due June 1, 2027.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.03 to C$109.18 to yield 6.001 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 26 basis points from 24 basis points at Friday's close.
